and_no_shipped_matmul_reaches_the_legacy.reading: every shipped matmul in all three model families, on HBM and on both ROM topologies, declares BF16 or FP8_E4M3FN operands and no block scale, so all 761 now satisfy use_pipe_mac.  The whole shipped matmul path runs on the 608.6 MHz lane and none of it runs on the 64.3 MHz one.
and_no_shipped_matmul_reaches_the_legacy.what_it_closes: the qualification this record raised against results/physical_abi3/asap7/limiter_ladder.json.  The ladder ranks blocks that have CLOSED, and ot_a3_mac_lane at 64.3 MHz was the reason to distrust it -- a block off the ladder carrying most of the shipped matmuls.  It carries none of them now, so the ladder describes the shipped token path as well as the closed set.
and_no_shipped_matmul_reaches_the_legacy.what_it_does_not_claim: that ot_a3_mac_lane is dead.  ot_a3_engine_array still instantiates it and still routes to it for a dtype pair the pipelined lane does not claim -- FP32, FP4, or any descriptor declaring a block scale -- so it remains the implementation of record for those and is exercised by the engine campaign's own cases.  What is measured here is that no SHIPPED descriptor is one of those.

answer: the slow one, almost entirely.  Of 272 TENSOR.MATMUL operators in the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash HBM cell, 26 are BF16 x BF16 and reach ot_a3_mac_lane_pipe at 394.0 MHz; the other 246 -- 90.4% -- involve FP8 and reach ot_a3_mac_lane, which routed at 64.3 MHz and did NOT meet a 4 ns target.  FIXED: the pipelined lane now decodes FP8 to BF16 exactly and the routing admits it, at a cost of 0.4% frequency.

measured_on.deployment: the published shipped V4.1 HBM c512 cell, 8 nodes

not_a_claim: that the change has been made: it has not.  This records where the leverage is and why the conversion is sound, measured on the shipped descriptors
that 394.0 MHz would survive an FP8 front end: a decode adds logic to the issue path and the routed number would have to be re-measured
that the legacy lane is wrong -- it is the certifying implementation and stays so; what this says is that the SHIPPED path does not reach the fast one
question: ot_a3_engine_array routes TENSOR.MATMUL between two lanes on the descriptor.  Which lane do the SHIPPED descriptors actually reach?

the_change_is_now_made.a_stale_record_found_while_doing_it: the committed 394.0 MHz record for this block is from commit 6700ef8b and a different source list; the same module without the FP8 path closes at 611.2 MHz today.  Both of today's records are filed so the comparison is one variable.
the_change_is_now_made.and_one_thing_the_gate_caught: the first attempt computed on a RESERVED E4M3FN encoding instead of refusing it.  ot_a3_format_pkg reports 0x7f and 0xff by setting FMT_ERR_NONFINITE and leaving the VALUE at zero, so narrowing the value handed the MAC a finite zero and the MAC had nothing to refuse -- matmul_fp8_reserved_encoding wanted fault 1 and got fault 0 with six words written. The lane now reads the decode TAG, delayed by the pipe's five stages and first in the legacy lane's refusal order, and the bench carries that case so it stays caught.
gated_by: rtl/test/tb_mac_lane_pipe_equiv.sv: 16 descriptors, five FP8 dtype pairings and four refusals, write streams and error codes IDENTICAL to the legacy lane, at 2.94x to 4.41x fewer cycles
tools/rtl_abi3_engine_campaign.py: pass on iverilog and verilator, 40,878 checks each, with the marker byte-identical to the run before the change
the_change_is_now_made.what: ot_a3_mac_lane_pipe decodes an FP8_E4M3FN operand to a BF16 code before the MAC, and ot_a3_engine_array's use_pipe_mac admits FP8 on either operand.  The block-scale condition is unchanged.
the_change_is_now_made.what_the_shipped_descriptors_get: the 246 FP8 matmuls move from ot_a3_mac_lane at 64.3 MHz, which did not meet a 4 ns target, to ot_a3_mac_lane_pipe at 608.6 MHz closed: 9.5x on 90.4% of the shipped matmuls

ot_a3_mac_lane.why: fp32_mul_rne and fp32_add_rne in series between registers, at S_MUL and S_ACC

the_routing_condition: ot_a3_engine_array.sv:527 -- use_pipe_mac requires cfg_dtype_a == BF16 AND cfg_dtype_b == BF16 AND no declared block scale on either operand
what_it_qualifies: results/physical_abi3/asap7/limiter_ladder.json ranks the blocks that have CLOSED, and on that basis no rung above 276.9 MHz is worth more than 1.098x.  ot_a3_mac_lane is not on that ladder because it has not closed -- and it carries 90.4% of the shipped matmuls.  The ladder is therefore a statement about the closed set and not about the shipped token path, and this record is the qualification it needs.

why_this_is_the_concentrated_lever.the_conversion_is_EXACT: FP8_E4M3FN has three mantissa bits and BF16 has seven, and E4M3FN's exponent range (2**-9 .. 448) sits inside BF16's, so every finite E4M3FN value is exactly representable in BF16.  ot_a3_format_pkg says as much for binary32 and exhaustively checks all 256 codes; the same argument gives BF16.  So a decode in front of the BF16 MAC is a REPRESENTATION change and not a numeric one.
why_this_is_the_concentrated_lever.the_scale_path_is_not_in_the_way: zero shipped matmuls declare a scale operand, so the other half of the routing condition is already satisfied by all 246
why_this_is_the_concentrated_lever.the_size_of_it: moving those 246 from 64.3 MHz to 394.0 MHz is 6.1x on the operator that dominates the token path, against the 1.024x that fixing the published limiter buys
